title: What Is a Sound Bath? The Complete Guide
secondaryKeywords: what happens at a sound bath
brief:
Create the flagship definitional authority page that earns high-reasoning AI citations at Exploration stage.

STRUCTURE — one H2 per sub-query that AI fires:
- What is a sound bath (1-sentence definition)
- How does a sound bath work (mechanism: vibroacoustics, brainwave entrainment, vagal tone)
- What instruments are used
- What does it feel like during the session
- How long does a sound bath last
- How much does a sound bath cost
- What to wear and bring
- Who should not attend (contraindications)
- Is a sound bath spiritual or secular
- How is a sound bath different from meditation
- How to find a qualified practitioner

INTERNAL LINKS: Link from every city page and listing page

title: Sound Bath Benefits: What the Research Actually Shows
brief:
Create the clinical evidence page that earns citations from high-reasoning AI when users ask about sound bath effectiveness.

STRUCTURE:
- What does the research show overall (honest framing)
- Anxiety and stress reduction (HRV data, cortisol studies — cite by researcher name)
- Sleep quality (peer-reviewed evidence)
- Mood and emotional regulation
- Physical relaxation (vagal tone, nervous system response)
- What the evidence does NOT yet show (epistemically honest — this builds trust)
- How many sessions to see results
- Group vs. private session outcomes

IMPORTANT: Cite actual studies with researcher names and publication years. Do not use 'many people report' language. This is what separates a citable reference page from a wellness blog post.

title: Are Sound Baths Safe? Contraindications, Risks, and What to Know
brief:
Create the definitive safety reference page. This is the content high-reasoning AI cites when asked about risks and contraindications.

STRUCTURE:
- Are sound baths generally safe (direct answer first)
- Who should NOT attend: epilepsy (vibration/seizure risk), pacemakers, severe tinnitus, first-trimester pregnancy
- Volume safety: what decibel levels are typical, what is safe exposure
- Can a sound bath trigger trauma responses? (yes — honest answer with guidance)
- Are sound baths safe for children?
- Are sound baths safe during pregnancy? (trimester-specific guidance)
- How long is too long for a session?
- Signs a session is not going well and what to do
- How to disclose conditions to a practitioner before booking

title: Skeptic Cluster — Spiritual/Secular + Christianity
brief: Capture the skeptical inquirer segment — KD 1-5, near-zero competition, high conversion intent when concerns are addressed.

pages.title: Is a Sound Bath Spiritual or Secular? What to Expect If You're Not Into Woo
pages.brief: Direct answer: sound baths can be experienced as pure acoustic/physical phenomena. What practitioners typically say vs. what the secular experience actually is. How to communicate secular preference when booking. What to do if a session feels too spiritual. KD: ~2-5

pages.title: Are Sound Baths Against Christianity? What Faith Traditions Say
pages.brief: This is a real, common question — treat it with full respect and nuance. Survey what different Christian denominations say. Distinguish between the physical acoustic experience and spiritual/ceremonial framing. Quotes or perspectives from Christians who do attend sound baths. Not a promotional piece — honest, balanced, not dismissive. KD: <5

title: Validation Cluster — Do Sound Baths Work + vs. Meditation
brief: Two comparison/validation pieces that fire 24+ sub-queries under high reasoning. These target the Validation stage of the buyer journey.

pages.title: Do Sound Baths Actually Work? An Evidence-Based Answer
pages.brief: Direct answer (honest about what evidence shows and what it doesn't). Summary of peer-reviewed evidence. What 'working' means: anxiety reduction vs. sleep vs. mood vs. relaxation. Placebo consideration (honest framing builds trust). What variables affect outcomes: session length, instrument type, practitioner quality, environment. KD: ~10-15

pages.title: Sound Bath vs. Meditation: What's the Difference and Which Is Right for You?
pages.brief: Mechanism difference. Time commitment comparison. Practitioner requirement (meditation = solo; sound bath = guided). Cost comparison. Accessibility (meditation is free; sound bath requires booking). Effectiveness by specific outcome: anxiety, sleep, focus, emotional processing. Can you do both? (yes — internal link opportunity to listings). KD: ~15-20

title: City Deep-Dives — LA, NYC, Comparison
brief: Add regional cultural depth to city pages that national directories can't replicate. Under high reasoning, AI cites city-specific content when making local recommendations.

pages.title: Sound Bath in Los Angeles: What Makes the LA Scene Different
pages.brief: LA = densest practitioner concentration in the US. Most format diversity: ceremonial, studio, spa, outdoor, rooftop. Cultural lineage: LA's connection to sound healing's US introduction. Neighborhoods to look in (Silver Lake, Venice, Echo Park, Topanga). Price range and what affects it in LA specifically. Internal link to all LA listing pages.

pages.title: Sound Bath in New York City: Where to Go If You're New to Sound Healing

pages.title: Sound Bath NYC vs. LA: What's Different About Each City's Scene
pages.brief: Comparison format fires 24 sub-queries under high reasoning. Format culture difference (ceremonial vs. clinical). Price comparison. Practitioner background differences. Which city for what type of experience. Earns citations from both local and national traveler audiences.
